blocks.title: Binary search
blocks.text: Binary search finds an item in a sorted list by repeatedly halving the search interval and discarding the half where the item cannot be, until the item is found or the interval is empty.

items: Start with the middle element of the sorted list.
If it is the target, return its position.
If the target is smaller, repeat on the left half.
If the target is larger, repeat on the right half.

blocks.text: In [1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13], a search for 7 starts at the middle element, 7, and finds it immediately. Binary search is O(log n), much faster than linear search for large datasets. It works only on sorted lists: sort unsorted data first, for example with merge sort (Tip).

blocks.alt: BINARY SEARCH: five copies of the sorted list 21, 34, 43, 57, 66, 78 with step notes. Search 78, divide from the middle and check mid (43); 78 > 43, look for 78 in the right half; new mid = 66, check mid; 78 > 66, look on the right half; new mid = 78, element found at mid (circled).
